intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a freefall of 8.5 seconds and is the ultimate adrenaline rush for thrill-seekers visiting Queenstown.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular one-day walks, crossing volcanic terrain with emerald crater lakes, steaming vents, and panoramic views of the Central Plateau. The 19.4km trail takes approximately 7-8 hours and is considered one of the world's best day hikes.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Guided Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the famous Routeburn Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks, through ancient beech forests and alpine meadows with stunning views of the Humboldt Mountains and Lake Mackenzie. A guided experience provides rich insights into the local flora, fauna, and Maori history.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungy site, the historic Kawarau Bridge. Jump 43 meters above the turquoise Kawarau River in a stunning gorge setting. This iconic AJ Hackett experience is perfect for first-timers and includes the option to touch the water.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: Walk the breathtaking Hooker Valley Track, a relatively easy 10km return hike through swing bridges and glacial valleys with jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, New Zealand's highest peak. The trail ends at the Hooker Glacier terminal lake filled with icebergs.
experiences.location: Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, Mackenzie District

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing

experiences.location: Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, Mackenzie District

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the budget-friendly Christchurch Metro Purple Line bus (approx. NZD $4) into the city centre. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a leisurely self-guided walk around Christchurch city centre - explore the Botanic Gardens (free entry) and the colourful container mall Re:START to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Avon River Precinct as the sun sets. Head to nearby Riverside Market for an affordable dinner from one of the food stalls - try a local burger or fish and chips for under NZD $15. Pick up snacks and supplies from a nearby Countdown supermarket for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap meat pie or sandwich from a New World or Pak'nSave supermarket near the airport for NZD $3-6
meals.dinner: Riverside Market food stalls in Christchurch city centre - budget NZD $12-18 for a filling meal

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Use this evening to rest, rehydrate, and prepare your gear for the active days ahead. Purchase a prepaid SIM card at the airport (Skinny Mobile is the most budget-friendly option, approx. NZD $20 with data). Download offline maps on Google Maps or Maps.me for the South Island.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the accommodation, then drive or take an InterCity bus south towards Lake Tekapo (approx. 3-hour drive or 3.5-hour bus). Enjoy the stunning Mackenzie Basin scenery en route. Arrive at Lake Tekapo and take a free walk along the lakeshore - the turquoise glacial waters are spectacular in the morning light. Visit the iconic Church of the Good Shepherd (free, exterior viewing).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up Mount John via the free forest trail (approx. 2-3 hours return, 360-degree panoramic views of the Mackenzie Basin and surrounding alps). This is a moderate hike with rewarding views and costs nothing. Pack a packed lunch to eat at the summit. Afterwards, cool your feet at the lake edge.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Tekapo Springs Hot Pools for a budget soak (approx. NZD $25-30) to relax your hiking muscles. Stargaze from the lakeshore after dark - Lake Tekapo is in a Dark Sky Reserve and the Milky Way is visible with the naked eye. Dinner at a local café or self-catered at your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at the accommodation - NZD $2-4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch prepared the night before - sandwiches, fruit, trail mix - NZD $5-8
meals.dinner: Mackenzie's Bar & Grill or Four Square supermarket self-catering in Tekapo - budget NZD $10-20

day_by_day.notes: InterCity bus from Christchurch to Lake Tekapo costs approx. NZD $25-40 if booked in advance. If you have a rental car, this gives more flexibility. Lake Tekapo has limited budget accommodation - book a hostel dorm (YHA or Tasman Holiday Parks) in advance for NZD $35-50/night.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and drive or bus from Lake Tekapo to Aoraki/Mount Cook Village (approx. 1.5 hours). This is one of New Zealand's most dramatic landscapes. Begin the Hooker Valley Track early in the morning when the light is golden and crowds are minimal. The 10km return trail crosses three swing bridges and passes Mueller Glacier Lake before reaching the Hooker Glacier viewpoint with jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the Hooker Valley Track and return to the village (allow 3-4 hours total). Have lunch at the village. If energy allows, take the short Kea Point Track (2 hours return, free) for additional glacier and mountain views from a different angle. Visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre museum (small entry fee approx. NZD $10) to learn about New Zealand's mountaineering history.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the last light on the Southern Alps from the village. Self-cater dinner at your accommodation or the basic camp kitchen. Stargaze from the Aoraki Mackenzie Dark Sky Reserve - one of the best stargazing spots on Earth. Return to Lake Tekapo accommodation or stay overnight at Mount Cook YHA (dorm from NZD $40).

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before the hike - muesli bars, banana, instant coffee - NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail or at the village - sandwiches and snacks - NZD $6-10
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or noodles at the camp kitchen - NZD $5-10

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is one of the featured experiences for this trip. It is free to walk and suitable for most fitness levels. Wear layers as mountain weather can change rapidly even in November. Start early (by 8am) to avoid afternoon clouds that often obscure the mountain views. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Mount Cook/Lake Tekapo region towards Queenstown (approx. 3.5-4 hour drive or bus). The InterCity bus route passes through stunning Mackenzie Country. Enjoy the scenery through the bus window. Arrive in Queenstown by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to budget accommodation in Queenstown (Base Backpackers or Nomads Queenstown hostel, dorm beds from NZD $35-45/night). Explore the Queenstown waterfront along Lake Wakatipu - it's free and beautiful. Walk up to Queenstown Hill (Te Tapu-nui) for panoramic views over the town and lake - a 2-hour return hike that costs nothing and rivals the gondola views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Queenstown town centre. Browse the Queenstown Night Market (runs Thursday to Sunday, free entry) for affordable street food options. Book your bungee jumping experience for the following day at AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge to lock in the best price. Enjoy the buzzing Queenstown atmosphere along the lakefront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered or included at hostel - NZD $0-8
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap falafel wrap or burger from one of the food trucks near the Queenstown waterfront - NZD $10-14
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market street food (Thursday-Sunday) or Fergburger takeaway for NZD $12-18 - a Queenstown institution

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown is the adventure capital of New Zealand and the base for your bungee jumping experience. Book AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy (NZD $185-220) or the cheaper Ledge Bungy (NZD $165) in advance online to secure your spot. Queenstown can be expensive - cook your own meals at the hostel kitchen as much as possible to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Today is your bungee jumping day! Head to AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy (43 metres, the world's first commercial bungy site) just 23km from Queenstown. The historic Kawarau Bridge setting over the turquoise river is iconic. Complete your jump in the morning when you are fresh and energised. Watch other jumpers before and after your turn. The experience including photos/video is available as a package.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown buzzing with adrenaline. Celebrate with lunch in town. In the afternoon, take the free Queenstown Gardens walk along the peninsula (1 hour, flat and easy). Alternatively, hike the Tiki Trail up to the Gondola summit (free, 1 hour steep hike) for spectacular 360-degree views over the Remarkables mountain range and Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Share your bungee jumping stories with fellow travellers at the hostel. Cook a budget meal at the hostel kitchen. Join a free hostel social event or head to Minus 5 Ice Bar for a look (entry from NZD $30 if budget allows). Early night to prepare for the next day's hiking adventure.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the jump - toast, banana, water - NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Treat yourself post-jump at a mid-range café - budget NZD $15-20 as a celebration
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the hostel kitchen - pasta, vegetables, canned tuna - NZD $8-12

day_by_day.notes: AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy costs approx. NZD $185-220 per person. This is the major splurge of the trip and a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Book directly on the AJ Hackett website for the best price and check for any online discount codes. A free shuttle from Queenstown town centre is often available. Minimum weight is 35kg, maximum 180kg. Wear comfortable, secure clothing and lace-up shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day hike from Queenstown - take the free Frankton Track or drive to the Bob's Peak area. For a more adventurous option, hike the Ben Lomond Track (full day, 11km return, 1748m summit) - one of Queenstown's best free hikes with extraordinary alpine views. Start early by 7-8am as it is a full day commitment. The trail starts from the Gondola base station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond summit hike or, if you took a shorter route, explore the Arrowtown historic gold mining village (30 minutes from Queenstown by bus or car). Arrowtown is free to explore and has a charming main street with 19th-century buildings. Walk the Arrow River trail and try gold panning at the river.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for the evening. Visit the Queenstown waterfront for sunset over the Remarkables. Dinner at the hostel or a budget-friendly option in town. Start planning and packing for the Milford Sound region.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at the hostel before the hike - NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail - energy bars, sandwiches, dried fruit - NZD $6-10
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the hostel or Pak'nSave supermarket meal deal - NZD $8-15

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Lomond Track is a challenging but rewarding full-day hike. Allow 6-8 hours for the full summit return. Bring at least 2 litres of water, sunscreen, a warm layer, and rain gear as alpine conditions can change quickly. The track is well-marked but steep in sections. Check the DOC (Department of Conservation) website for track conditions before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the drive or bus to Te Anau (approx. 2-2.5 hours from Queenstown). Te Anau is the gateway to Fiordland National Park and Milford Sound. Check in to Te Anau YHA or Barnyard Backpackers (dorm from NZD $35-45). Explore the Te Anau lakefront and township. Visit the free DOC Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre to learn about the region's ecology and get updated track information.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the free Kepler Track Day Walk - take the short section from the Te Anau Control Gates along the lake edge and into the beech forest (2-3 hours return, flat and easy). Alternatively, rent a bike from a local shop (approx. NZD $25-35/day) and cycle the lakefront trail. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves boat tour (NZD $55-75) if budget allows - a magical underground experience.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare your packed lunch for the Milford Sound day trip tomorrow. Cook dinner at the hostel kitchen. Chat with fellow travellers about the Milford Sound experience. Early bedtime as tomorrow requires a very early start.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hostel - NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Te Anau town café or supermarket - budget NZD $10-15
meals.dinner: Self-catered hostel kitchen meal - pasta, sauce, salad - NZD $8-12

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau is a small, relatively affordable town compared to Queenstown. Stock up on groceries at the Four Square supermarket for the next 2 days. Book your Milford Sound cruise in advance online - the cheapest options are the budget nature cruises from Real Journeys or Jucy Cruize (approx. NZD $65-85). The drive to Milford Sound is 2.5 hours each way from Te Anau.

day_by_day.morning: Very early start (depart Te Anau by 7am). Drive or take a budget bus to Milford Sound through the stunning Fiordland scenery. Stop at Mirror Lakes (free, 5-minute walk) and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain along the way. Arrive at Milford Sound and board your pre-booked budget nature cruise. The 2-hour cruise takes you past Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and Bowen Falls with views of fur seals and dolphins.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cruise, explore the Milford Sound foreshore and take the free short walk to the Bowen Falls base (20 minutes return). Begin the drive back towards Te Anau, stopping at the Chasm Walk (free, 20-minute loop) to see the dramatic water-carved rock formations. Arrive back in Te Anau by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and recover at the hostel after a long but incredible day. Share Milford Sound photos and stories. Self-cater a simple dinner at the hostel kitchen. Plan the next day's activities.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast before departure - muesli bars and fruit - NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the cruise or at Milford Sound - NZD $0 (prepared the night before)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the hostel - NZD $8-12

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound is one of New Zealand's most iconic destinations and a must-see. The road to Milford Sound (State Highway 94) is one of the most scenic drives in the world. November is a great time to visit as waterfalls are at their peak flow. Be prepared for sandflies (small biting insects) at Milford Sound - bring insect repellent. The budget cruise option still provides spectacular views.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning in Te Anau. Walk the Te Anau Lakefront Track (flat, easy, free) for morning views across the lake to the Fiordland mountains. Visit the DOC Te Anau Bird Sanctuary (free) to see the rare takahē, a flightless bird once thought extinct. Browse the small Te Anau township.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Te Anau back towards the West Coast via State Highway 6 (approx. 3-4 hours drive) or take a scenic route through Lumsden and Gore towards Dunedin (approx. 3-3.5 hours). Alternatively, if heading to the West Coast, stop at Haast Pass for stunning mountain and river scenery. Arrive at your next destination and check in.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your next accommodation. If in Dunedin, explore the Octagon city centre (free). If on the West Coast, enjoy the wild beach scenery. Self-cater dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hostel in Te Anau - NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the road journey - NZD $5-8
meals.dinner: Self-catered at new accommodation or a local budget café - NZD $10-18

day_by_day.notes: Day 9 is a travel day between regions. The South Island requires significant driving between attractions. If using public transport, InterCity buses connect Te Anau to Dunedin (approx. NZD $30-50). Consider splitting the journey with a stop at the Catlins region if heading to Dunedin - the Catlins has free waterfalls and wildlife viewing.

day_by_day.morning: If in Dunedin: Visit the Otago Peninsula for free wildlife viewing. Drive or cycle to Sandfly Bay for a free New Zealand sea lion encounter on the beach (DOC reserve, free entry). Hike the short ridge walk above Sandfly Bay for panoramic coastal views. This is one of the best free wildlife experiences in New Zealand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Otago Peninsula further - visit the free Taiaroa Head Royal Albatross Colony viewing area (the colony itself costs NZD $55 but the surrounding area is free). Drive back along the peninsula and stop at Larnach Castle grounds (free to walk around the exterior). Return to Dunedin city and walk up to the Baldwin Street lookout (the world's steepest residential street, free).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Dunedin's vibrant student city atmosphere. Visit the Dunedin Railway Station (free to admire the exterior architecture). Dinner at one of Dunedin's affordable student-friendly cafés or restaurants on George Street. Try the famous Dunedin café culture.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hostel - NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Sandfly Bay or Otago Peninsula - NZD $5-8
meals.dinner: George Street café or restaurant in Dunedin - budget NZD $15-22

day_by_day.notes: Dunedin (Ōtepoti) is one of New Zealand's most affordable cities with a strong student population keeping prices reasonable. The Otago Peninsula is spectacular and almost entirely free to explore. November is breeding season for sea lions at Sandfly Bay - maintain a respectful distance of at least 20 metres from all wildlife. Dunedin Backpackers or Hogwartz Backpackers offer dorm beds from NZD $30-40.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Dunedin north along the scenic coastal route towards Christchurch (approx. 3.5-4 hours). Stop at Moeraki Boulders (NZD $5 parking fee) - extraordinary spherical boulders on the beach that look like giant alien eggs. Walk along the beach and photograph these geological wonders. Continue north through Oamaru.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Oamaru to explore the free Victorian Precinct - a beautifully preserved 19th-century harbour district with limestone buildings. Visit the free Oamaru Blue Penguin Colony viewing area at dusk (the paid evening penguin parade is NZD $35-45 but worth it if budget allows). Continue to Christchurch or stay overnight in Oamaru at a budget hostel.
day_by_day.evening: If continuing to Christchurch: arrive by early evening and settle back into your Christchurch accommodation. If staying in Oamaru: watch the Little Blue Penguins come ashore at the free public viewing area at dusk (penguins return from the sea between 7-9pm in November). Self-cater dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure - NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Fish and chips at Moeraki village or Oamaru - a classic NZ experience for NZD $10-15
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation or a budget café in Oamaru/Christchurch - NZD $10-18

day_by_day.notes: The Moeraki Boulders are a fascinating natural attraction. Visit at low tide for the best access and photography. Oamaru is a charming and underrated town with free Victorian architecture to explore. The Little Blue Penguins returning to shore at dusk is a magical free experience - bring a warm layer as it can be cool by the ocean in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Christchurch for the final full day. Spend the morning exploring Christchurch's remarkable post-earthquake recovery story. Visit the free Cardboard Cathedral (Te Hononga) - an extraordinary transitional cathedral made largely of cardboard tubes. Walk through the Bridge of Remembrance and explore the Gap Filler creative urban installations throughout the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Canterbury Museum to learn about South Island history, Māori culture, and Antarctic exploration. Walk through the Christchurch Botanic Gardens (free) - 30 hectares of beautiful gardens along the Avon River. Rent a punt on the Avon River for a relaxing afternoon (approx. NZD $25-35 for 30 minutes). Visit the Transitional City art installations.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in New Zealand. Splurge slightly on a nice farewell dinner at a mid-range Christchurch restaurant on Oxford Terrace or New Regent Street. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Reflect on the incredible 13-day South Island adventure.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the accommodation - NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Riverside Market food hall in Christchurch - NZD $12-18
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range restaurant on New Regent Street - budget NZD $25-35 as a final celebration

day_by_day.notes: Christchurch (Ōtautahi) has undergone a remarkable transformation since the 2011 earthquake. The city's creative and resilient spirit is inspiring. Use this final full day to pick up any last-minute New Zealand souvenirs from the Christchurch Arts Centre markets. Confirm your departure flight details and arrange airport transport. The Metro Purple Line bus to the airport costs NZD $4 and takes approximately 30 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand. Check out of accommodation and head to Christchurch Airport. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your international departure for check-in and security. Enjoy a final flat white coffee at the airport - New Zealand's coffee culture is world-class. Reflect on an incredible budget adventure through the South Island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Christchurch International Airport. Safe travels!
day_by_day.evening: In transit

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the accommodation before checkout or at the airport - NZD $5-15
meals.lunch: Airport meal or in-flight meal
meals.dinner: In-flight or at transit airport

day_by_day.notes: Departure day. Ensure you have completed any required New Zealand customs declarations. New Zealand has very strict biosecurity rules - dispose of any fruit, nuts, seeds, or plant material before passing through customs. Keep your accommodation receipts and activity tickets as memories of the trip. The NZD $35 International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) should have been paid when purchasing your visa or NZT entry approval prior to travel.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and rent a car for the trip. Drive to Queenstown (approx. 4.5 hours via SH1 and SH8), stopping at Lake Tekapo for a quick stretch and photos of the turquoise glacial lake and Church of the Good Shepherd along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Queenstown and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and take a leisurely stroll along the Queenstown waterfront on Lake Wakatipu to get your bearings. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of the town center.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Christchurch Airport or a roadside café in Geraldine on the drive south — try a classic Kiwi meat pie and flat white coffee (~NZD $15)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant on The Mall, Queenstown — celebrated farm-to-table New Zealand cuisine in a relaxed atmosphere. Budget around NZD $55–70 per person for mains and a glass of local Central Otago Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your rental car is booked in advance. Fill up on fuel before leaving Christchurch as some stretches between towns are remote. November is the start of New Zealand summer — expect long daylight hours (sunset around 9:00 PM) and generally warm, pleasant weather, though mountain areas can be unpredictable.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with the iconic Kawarau Bridge Bungy (43m) — the world's first commercial bungy site, just 23km from Queenstown. Book the 9:00 AM slot to beat crowds. Watch others jump while you gear up, then take the plunge above the stunning Kawarau River gorge. The on-site café is great for a pre-jump coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and explore the Queenstown Gardens — a beautiful free park on a peninsula with rose gardens, disc golf, and lake views. Rent a bike from outside the gardens and cycle the easy Queenstown Trail along the lakefront toward Frankton (~10km round trip, flat and scenic).
day_by_day.evening: Take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic sunset views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range. Try a luge run or two before sunset. Dine at the Skyline Restaurant buffet with 360-degree views, or head back down for dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Vudu Café & Larder on Rees Street — excellent eggs benedict and house-baked pastries. Budget NZD $20–28.
meals.lunch: Fergburger on Shotover Street — Queenstown's legendary burger institution. Try the 'Big Al' or 'Sweet Bambi' venison burger. Budget NZD $15–20.
meals.dinner: Skyline Restaurant buffet (NZD $65–75 per person including gondola) OR The Bunker on Cow Lane for a cozy mid-range dinner with craft cocktails and New Zealand lamb (~NZD $50–65 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Kawarau Bridge Bungy costs approximately NZD $185 per person — book online in advance through AJ Hackett to secure your preferred time slot and save 10%. The gondola costs NZD $36 return without luge. Wear comfortable shoes for the bike ride.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Glenorchy (45 minutes from Queenstown along a stunning lakeside road) for the Routeburn Track Guided Day Hike. Meet your guide at the Routeburn trailhead and begin the hike through ancient beech forests and alpine meadows. The guided section covers the lower valley with incredible views of the Harris Mountains and glacier-carved terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Routeburn guided hike into the afternoon, reaching viewpoints above the treeline. The guide will share insights on local flora, fauna, and Māori history of the region. Return to the trailhead by mid-afternoon. Stop in Glenorchy village for a well-earned rest at the Glenorchy Café.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Queenstown along the scenic Paradise Road if time permits, watching for deer and native birds. Back in Queenstown, relax at the resort. Optional: soak tired legs at the hotel or explore the lively Queenstown Night Market (held on Thursdays — note for later in the trip).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or pack snacks from a Queenstown supermarket (Countdown on Gorge Road) the night before — trail mix, energy bars, and fruit for the hike.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the guided hike operator (confirm when booking) OR bring your own packed lunch from the resort. Eat with stunning alpine views.
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant on Cow Lane — Queenstown institution famous for wood-fired pizzas and pasta in a rustic stone cottage setting. Budget NZD $35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track Guided Day Hike costs approximately NZD $195–230 per person. Wear sturdy hiking boots and bring waterproof layers — alpine weather can change rapidly even in November. The drive to Glenorchy is one of the most scenic in New Zealand and is worth taking slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Take on the Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. The AJ Hackett shuttle departs from central Queenstown at 8:30 AM. The pod suspended over the gorge is an experience in itself before you even jump. This is a true bucket-list adrenaline moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, recover with a gentle afternoon activity. Visit the Queenstown Hill Time Walk — a 2-hour return hike from town up to a summit basket sculpture with panoramic views of the entire Queenstown basin, Lake Wakatipu, and surrounding ranges. Free and accessible directly from town.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a well-deserved relaxation evening. Visit Onsen Hot Pools in Arthurs Point (15 minutes from Queenstown) — private outdoor hot tubs perched over the Shotover River gorge. Book a 1-hour private pool session. Then head to dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Eichardt's Bar on Marine Parade — elegant lakefront café with excellent eggs and avocado toast. Budget NZD $22–30. Eat before the shuttle pickup.
meals.lunch: Queenstown Farmers Market (held Saturdays — adjust if needed) or grab a gourmet sandwich and juice from Patagonia Chocolates & Ice Cream on Beach Street. Budget NZD $15.
meals.dinner: Finz Seafood & Grill on The Steamer Wharf — lakefront dining with fresh South Island seafood. Try the blue cod or green-lipped mussels. Budget NZD $50–65 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy costs approximately NZD $275 per person including shuttle — book online well in advance as slots fill up fast in summer. The Onsen Hot Pools cost NZD $55–75 per person for a 1-hour private pool — book ahead at onsen.co.nz. Combine the two experiences for a perfect adrenaline-to-relaxation day arc.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Arrowtown (20 minutes from Queenstown) — a beautifully preserved 1860s gold rush town. Walk the charming tree-lined main street, browse boutique shops and galleries, and visit the Lakes District Museum to learn about the region's gold mining and Chinese settler history (entry NZD $10).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Arrow River Bridges Trail from Arrowtown — a 4km loop following the Arrow River through a gorge with historic swing bridges, old mining relics, and native bush. Alternatively, continue to Macetown, a ghost town reachable via a 4WD track or a longer 3-hour return hike through the river gorge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown in time for the famous Queenstown Thursday Night Market on the waterfront. Browse local food stalls, artisan crafts, and street performers. This is the perfect casual evening with great food variety at budget-friendly prices.

meals.breakfast: Provisions of Arrowtown on Buckingham Street — award-winning café with legendary eggs, house-made granola, and specialty coffee. Budget NZD $20–28.
meals.lunch: Picnic by the Arrow River using supplies from the Arrowtown village shops, or try Slow Cuts in Arrowtown for excellent sandwiches and salads. Budget NZD $15–20.
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market food stalls — sample a variety of cuisines including New Zealand lamb skewers, wood-fired pizza, Asian dumplings, and fresh churros. Budget NZD $20–30 for a full grazing dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is particularly beautiful in autumn (April–May) but is equally lovely in November with spring blooms. The Arrow River Bridges Trail is well-marked and suitable for all fitness levels. Wear light layers as temperatures can vary between the valley and open areas.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Te Anau (2 hours from Queenstown via SH6). Check in to a Te Anau accommodation or store luggage, then head straight to the Kepler Track for a half-day section hike. Walk from the Te Anau control gates along the lakeshore to Brod Bay — a beautiful 3-hour return walk through beech forest with stunning lake views (free, no bookings required).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves — a must-do experience. Take the boat across Lake Te Anau and explore the cave system with its underground whirlpool, waterfalls, and magical glowworm grotto. Tours depart regularly from the Real Journeys office in Te Anau. Duration: approximately 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming lakeside town of Te Anau. Walk the lakefront promenade at sunset. Visit the Te Anau Bird Sanctuary (free) to see the rare takahē — a flightless bird once thought extinct. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure, or stop at a Queenstown café for takeaway coffee and pastries for the road.
meals.lunch: Miles Better Pies in Te Anau — legendary local pie shop with Fiordland-themed fillings including venison and blue cod. Budget NZD $8–12.
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant & Bar on Mokonui Street, Te Anau — beloved local restaurant in a historic cottage serving Fiordland venison, lamb, and fresh fish. Budget NZD $45–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau Glowworm Caves tours cost approximately NZD $89 per person — book through Real Journeys (realjourneys.co.nz) in advance as tours sell out. This is a transition day moving from Queenstown to the Fiordland region. The drive via Kingston and the Mossburn plains is scenic and worth taking slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the drive to Milford Sound (1.5 hours from Te Anau via the stunning Milford Road). Stop at the Mirror Lakes, Eglinton Valley, and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain along the way. Walk through the Homer Tunnel and descend into the dramatic Milford Sound valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a Milford Sound cruise — the iconic way to experience the fiord. Sail past Mitre Peak (1,692m), Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls, and through to the Tasman Sea. Keep an eye out for bottlenose dolphins, New Zealand fur seals, and Fiordland crested penguins. A 2-hour cruise covers the full fiord.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau (1.5 hours). Stop at the Chasm walk near the Cleddau River — a short 20-minute return walk to dramatic water-sculpted rock formations. Arrive back in Te Anau for a relaxed evening by the lake.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Te Anau accommodation or pack supplies the night before — eat at the Mirror Lakes picnic area with stunning reflections.
meals.lunch: Milford Sound Lodge Café at the sound — enjoy a hot meal or packed lunch with views of the fiord. Budget NZD $20–30.
meals.dinner: Fiordland Hotel & Motel's restaurant on Lakefront Drive, Te Anau — casual lakeside dining with classic New Zealand comfort food. Budget NZD $35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound cruises cost approximately NZD $85–120 per person — book through Real Journeys or Go Orange in advance. November is an excellent time to visit Milford Sound as waterfalls are full from spring snowmelt. Sandflies are present near the water — bring insect repellent. Depart Te Anau by 7:30 AM to make the most of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau to Wanaka (2.5 hours via Queenstown or 3 hours via the scenic Crown Range Road). If taking the Crown Range Road, stop at the Cardrona Valley viewpoint. Arrive in Wanaka and check in or store luggage. Walk the Wanaka lakefront and visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' — the lone willow growing in the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Roy's Peak Track — Wanaka's most iconic hike with a 1,578m summit offering breathtaking 360-degree views of Lake Wanaka, Mount Aspiring, and the surrounding Southern Alps. The track is 16km return with 1,200m elevation gain — allow 5–6 hours total. Start no later than 1:00 PM for a late afternoon summit.
day_by_day.evening: Descend Roy's Peak and drive back to Wanaka. Rest and freshen up. Wander along Wanaka's charming lakefront at golden hour — the light on the mountains is spectacular. Enjoy a well-earned dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Te Anau café before departure, or pack food for the road.
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch and plenty of water for the Roy's Peak hike — eat at the summit with one of New Zealand's most spectacular views.
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen on Helwick Street, Wanaka — beloved local Italian restaurant with handmade pasta and wood-fired pizzas. Budget NZD $35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is a challenging hike — wear proper hiking boots and bring sun protection, as there is minimal shade. The track can be crowded at the famous Instagram viewpoint — arrive early or late to avoid queues for photos. November weather in Wanaka is generally warm and sunny but afternoon thunderstorms are possible — check the forecast before starting.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Wanaka township at a relaxed pace. Visit Puzzling World — a quirky attraction with optical illusions, a fascinating puzzle centre, and the famous tilted building. Great for a fun 1.5-hour visit. Then browse the boutique shops and galleries along Ardmore Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Loop — a 3.5-hour, 6km circuit near Wanaka with two distinct lake views, a waterfall, and panoramic summit views of Lake Wanaka and the Southern Alps. A hidden gem compared to the busier Roy's Peak.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at Pembroke Patisserie & Café on the lakefront, watching the alpenglow on the mountains. Then head to Wanaka's vibrant restaurant strip for dinner. Consider visiting Cinema Paradiso — Wanaka's iconic boutique cinema in old couches and armchairs for a late movie screening.

meals.breakfast: Federal Diner on Dunmore Street, Wanaka — excellent brunch spot with smashed avo, eggs, and specialty coffee. Budget NZD $20–28.
meals.lunch: Kika on Helwick Street — modern New Zealand café with seasonal small plates and excellent coffee. Budget NZD $20–30.
meals.dinner: Ritual Café & Bar on Ardmore Street — relaxed lakefront bar and restaurant with craft beers, shared plates, and New Zealand beef burgers. Budget NZD $30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Puzzling World entry costs approximately NZD $22 per adult. Diamond Lake Track is free and well-signposted from the Mt Aspiring Road, about 20 minutes drive from Wanaka town. Cinema Paradiso is a uniquely New Zealand experience — check their schedule at cinemawanaka.co.nz. Intermission includes freshly baked cookies.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Wanaka to Franz Josef Glacier (3.5 hours via the Haast Pass — one of New Zealand's most spectacular mountain passes). Stop at Haast Pass viewpoint, Thunder Creek Falls (a 5-minute walk to a 28m waterfall), and the Blue Pools near Makarora — a stunning 45-minute return walk to crystal-clear blue swimming holes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Franz Josef village. Check in to accommodation and head to the Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — a 1.5-hour return walk through the glacier valley to the glacier viewpoint. The glacier has retreated significantly but the valley views and ice cliffs are still dramatic and impressive.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the tiny village of Franz Josef. Visit the West Coast Wildlife Centre to see live kiwi birds in a nocturnal house (a rare and magical experience). Enjoy dinner at one of the village restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — pack breakfast from Wanaka supermarket or eat at the resort before leaving.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at the Blue Pools or at a Haast Pass rest area — bring supplies from Wanaka. Alternatively, stop at the Haast River Café in Haast village.
meals.dinner: Alice May Restaurant & Bar in Franz Josef — the best restaurant in the village with great venison, lamb, and West Coast whitebait dishes. Budget NZD $40–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass route (SH6) is one of the great scenic drives of New Zealand — allow extra time for stops. Fuel up in Wanaka as petrol stations are sparse between Wanaka and Franz Josef. West Coast Wildlife Centre entry costs approximately NZD $35 per adult — the kiwi encounter is well worth it. Book in advance at wildkiwi.co.nz.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Franz Josef Glacier Heli-Hike — fly by helicopter to the upper glacier and hike on the ice with crampons and an expert guide for 2–3 hours. This is a spectacular way to experience the glacier up close, exploring ice caves, crevasses, and seracs. Book the 9:00 AM departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive north to Hokitika (1.5 hours from Franz Josef). Visit Hokitika Gorge — a 30-minute drive inland leads to a stunning turquoise gorge with a swing bridge and easy 30-minute loop walk. The electric blue water colour is extraordinary. Then explore Hokitika town and the famous Hokitika Gorge Scenic Reserve.
day_by_day.evening: Browse Hokitika's renowned pounamu (greenstone/jade) galleries and workshops on Tancred Street — watch local carvers at work and consider purchasing a piece of authentic New Zealand greenstone as a souvenir. Drive back to Franz Josef or stay overnight in Hokitika.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Franz Josef Glacier Hotel café before the heli-hike.
meals.lunch: Hokitika Sandwich Bar on Revell Street — fresh local sandwiches and Westland whitebait fritters. Budget NZD $15–20.
meals.dinner: Stumpers Bar & Café in Franz Josef — casual pub atmosphere with hearty West Coast meals, local craft beer, and great value. Budget NZD $30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Franz Josef Glacier Heli-Hike costs approximately NZD $480–560 per person — this is a splurge but an absolute once-in-a-lifetime experience. Book through Franz Josef Glacier Guides (franzjosefglacier.com). Helicopter flights are weather-dependent — have a flexible backup plan. Hokitika whitebait fritters are a West Coast delicacy not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Franz Josef south back toward Queenstown via the Haast Pass (or fly if budget allows). Alternatively, if staying near Queenstown, drive to Mount Cook National Park (3.5 hours from Queenstown via Twizel). Arrive at Aoraki/Mount Cook Village and begin the Hooker Valley Track — a breathtaking 10km return hike through swing bridges past Mueller Lake to the Hooker Glacier terminal lake with direct views of Aoraki/Mount Cook (3,724m), New Zealand's highest peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the Hooker Valley Track (allow 3–4 hours return). The track passes three swing bridges and ends at a glacial lake with floating icebergs and a dramatic mountain backdrop. This is one of the most rewarding walks in New Zealand for the relatively easy effort required. Explore the Aoraki/Mount Cook Visitor Centre.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Queenstown (2.5 hours from Mount Cook via Twizel and Lake Pukaki). Stop at Lake Pukaki lookout for sunset — the turquoise lake with Aoraki/Mount Cook reflected in the water is one of the iconic images of New Zealand. Arrive back in Queenstown for the final overnight stay.

meals.breakfast: Pack an early breakfast or stop at the Old Mountaineers' Café in Mount Cook Village — legendary climbers' café with great coffee and hearty meals.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Hooker Valley Track — eat at the glacier terminal lake with Mount Cook towering above you for an unforgettable picnic.
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery on Marine Parade, Queenstown — upscale lakefront restaurant with premium New Zealand beef and lamb. A fitting celebratory final dinner. Budget NZD $65–85 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is free and well-maintained — suitable for most fitness levels with only 150m elevation gain. Wear sun protection as UV levels are very high in the Mount Cook basin. The Lake Pukaki lookout on SH8 is one of the most photographed spots in New Zealand — plan your timing for golden hour light on the mountains.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last walk along the lakefront. Visit the Queenstown Arts Centre or browse the Remarkables Market (if held on this day). Pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Drive to Christchurch Airport (4.5 hours) or Queenstown Airport for your departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: If departing from Queenstown Airport (15 minutes from town), allow 2 hours before your flight. If departing from Christchurch, begin the scenic drive north through the Mackenzie Basin, stopping at Lake Tekapo one final time for photos and a coffee at the Kohan Japanese Restaurant with lake views.
day_by_day.evening: Depart New Zealand with incredible memories of bungy jumps, glacier hikes, fiords, and some of the world's most spectacular landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Bespoke Kitchen on Isle Street, Queenstown — beautiful café with healthy bowls, eggs, and excellent coffee for a final South Island breakfast. Budget NZD $22–30.
meals.lunch: Airport café or a quick stop in Geraldine (on the Christchurch drive) at The Barker's of Geraldine café — famous for their fruit preserves and pies. Budget NZD $15–20.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Return your rental car at the airport — allow extra time for the return process. Queenstown Airport has excellent shopping for last-minute New Zealand souvenirs including manuka honey, pounamu jewellery, and Whittaker's chocolate. New Zealand biosecurity is strict — consume or dispose of all fresh food before departing. Keep your bungy jump certificate and heli-hike photos as lifelong mementos!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a freefall of 8.5 seconds and is the ultimate adrenaline rush for thrill-seekers visiting Queenstown.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular one-day walks, crossing volcanic terrain with emerald crater lakes, steaming vents, and panoramic views of the Central Plateau. The 19.4km trail takes approximately 7-8 hours and is considered one of the world's best day hikes.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Guided Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the famous Routeburn Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks, through ancient beech forests and alpine meadows with stunning views of the Humboldt Mountains and Lake Mackenzie. A guided experience provides rich insights into the local flora, fauna, and Maori history.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungy site, the historic Kawarau Bridge. Jump 43 meters above the turquoise Kawarau River in a stunning gorge setting. This iconic AJ Hackett experience is perfect for first-timers and includes the option to touch the water.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: Walk the breathtaking Hooker Valley Track, a relatively easy 10km return hike through swing bridges and glacial valleys with jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, New Zealand's highest peak. The trail ends at the Hooker Glacier terminal lake filled with icebergs.
experiences.location: Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, Mackenzie District

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands and clears customs/immigration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity from the resort. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to orient yourself and soak in the stunning South Island coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine dining restaurant. Unwind with a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir on your private terrace as the sun sets over the water.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: Light refreshments arranged by your private transfer service or a quick bite at the airport's premium lounge
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — indulge in a tasting menu featuring South Island seafood, Canterbury lamb, and locally sourced seasonal produce paired with a curated New Zealand wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep it relaxed. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the resort concierge. Request an early morning wake-up call schedule and any dietary preferences to be noted for the duration of the stay. Jet lag management: light meal, hydration, and early to bed recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort overlooking the beachfront. After breakfast, take a guided nature walk along the coastal trail near the resort — arranged through the concierge — to gently ease into South Island's dramatic landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day scenic helicopter tour over the surrounding region, including aerial views of glaciers, fiords, and mountain ranges. Land at a remote alpine location for a champagne picnic prepared by the resort's chef.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a spa treatment at the on-site luxury spa — choose from a deep tissue massage or a signature New Zealand manuka honey body wrap. Dinner at a premium local restaurant recommended by the concierge.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet buffet and à la carte breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — freshly baked pastries, local cheeses, smoked salmon, eggs cooked to order, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Private champagne alpine picnic during the helicopter excursion — artisan sandwiches, charcuterie, seasonal fruit, and sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated local fine dining establishment — expect dishes such as pan-seared blue cod, venison loin, and artisan New Zealand cheese boards

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour well in advance through the resort concierge. Weather permitting — have a backup indoor activity such as a private wine tasting or cooking class ready. Spa treatments should be booked upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort, then depart by private luxury vehicle toward Queenstown — the adventure capital of New Zealand and home to world-class bungy experiences. Enjoy the scenic drive through South Island's stunning landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience the iconic Kawarau Bridge Bungy — the world's first commercial bungy site, jumping 43 meters above the turquoise Kawarau River. A landmark adrenaline experience with historic significance. After the jump, explore Queenstown's boutique shops and waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Queenstown's finest restaurants overlooking Lake Wakatipu. Enjoy a post-adrenaline celebratory cocktail at a rooftop bar before returning to the resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, freshly squeezed juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside café lunch near the Kawarau Bridge — gourmet burgers, fresh salads, and craft beers or kombucha
meals.dinner: Queenstown fine dining — Amisfield Winery & Bistro or Rata Restaurant, featuring seasonal South Island ingredients with an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Kawarau Bridge Bungy must be pre-booked through AJ Hackett Bungy. Wear comfortable, athletic clothing. Weight limits apply (min 45kg, max 180kg). Private return transfer from Queenstown to the resort should be arranged in advance. Allow approximately 2 hours for the drive each way.

day_by_day.morning: Gourmet breakfast at the resort. Morning at leisure — enjoy the resort's beachfront infinity pool, kayak along the coastline, or take a private yoga session arranged by the concierge on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour to a nearby premium winery for an exclusive behind-the-scenes cellar tour and vertical tasting of Central Otago Pinot Noir vintages, paired with artisan local cheeses and charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise along the coastline on a chartered private vessel, with canapés and champagne. Return to the resort for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — avocado toast on sourdough, poached eggs, fresh fruit platters, and single-origin espresso
meals.lunch: Winery paired tasting lunch — artisan cheese boards, house-cured meats, fresh bread, and Pinot Noir pairings
meals.dinner: In-resort fine dining — try the chef's special tasting menu with optional wine pairing, featuring the evening's freshest local catch and seasonal vegetables

day_by_day.notes: A rest and indulgence day to balance the adventure-heavy schedule. The private winery visit should be pre-arranged through the concierge. Sunset cruise timing depends on the season — confirm departure time to align with golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Early gourmet breakfast, then depart by private luxury vehicle to Mount Cook / Aoraki National Park. Begin the breathtaking Hooker Valley Track — a 10km return hike through swing bridges, glacial rivers, and dramatic alpine scenery, culminating in views of the Mueller Glacier and the iconic face of Aoraki/Mount Cook.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the Hooker Valley Track and enjoy a packed gourmet picnic lunch at the glacier viewpoint. Return to the trailhead and take a short scenic drive to explore the surrounding national park before heading back toward the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a soothing post-hike soak in the resort's outdoor hot tub or a private bath drawn with local essential oils. Dinner at the resort with a focus on restorative, protein-rich dishes.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at the resort — granola, Greek yogurt, poached eggs, whole grain toast, and fresh fruit to fuel the hike
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed picnic prepared by the resort chef — smoked salmon wraps, quinoa salad, energy bars, fresh fruit, and thermos of premium tea or coffee
meals.dinner: Resort dinner — Canterbury rack of lamb, roasted root vegetables, and a glass of Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Hooker Valley Track is approximately 10km return and takes 3–4 hours at a comfortable pace. Wear sturdy hiking boots and bring layers — alpine weather can change rapidly. Sunscreen and sunglasses essential. The drive from the resort to Mount Cook is approximately 2–3 hours — depart by 7:00am. Pre-book the gourmet picnic with the resort kitchen the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Gourmet breakfast at the resort. Depart by private vehicle to Queenstown for the ultimate adrenaline experience — the legendary Nevis Bungy Jump. At 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge, this is New Zealand's highest bungy platform, offering 8.5 seconds of freefall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-jump celebration with a private Queenstown food and wine tour — visit artisan producers, sample local delicacies, and explore the vibrant Queenstown food scene. Browse boutique stores in the CBD.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails at a Queenstown rooftop bar with panoramic Lake Wakatipu views, followed by a premium dinner. Private luxury transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: High-energy breakfast at the resort — protein-packed eggs, avocado, whole grain toast, smoothies, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Queenstown artisan food tour — tastings at local producers including cheeses, charcuterie, craft chocolate, and paired wines
meals.dinner: Queenstown's premier restaurant — Botswana Butchery or The Bunker, featuring prime New Zealand beef, fresh seafood, and an award-winning wine list

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy must be pre-booked through AJ Hackett Bungy. A shuttle from Queenstown to the Nevis platform is included in the booking. Weight requirements: 45kg–127kg. Avoid heavy meals immediately before the jump. Bring a change of clothes — the adrenaline rush can be intense. GoPro footage packages available for purchase on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning. Enjoy a late, indulgent breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning relaxing on the beachfront, reading, or enjoying a private guided meditation session arranged by the concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided sea kayaking experience along the coastline — explore hidden coves, sea caves, and marine wildlife in a premium guided setting. Equipment and instruction provided.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beachfront dinner — the resort arranges a private table on the sand with a customized menu, candlelight, and a dedicated sommelier. A truly memorable South Island evening.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late breakfast — eggs royale, freshly baked croissants, berry compote, premium cheeses, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at the resort — fresh prawn salad, cold-pressed juices, and artisan bread
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner curated by the resort's executive chef — whole roasted fish, seasonal vegetables, and a bespoke wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Recovery and relaxation day after two high-adrenaline bungy experiences. Sea kayaking is a great low-impact activity — suitable for all fitness levels. Confirm the private beachfront dinner setup with the concierge at least 24 hours in advance. Weather contingency plan: indoor private dining room with ocean views.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the resort. Depart by private luxury vehicle toward the Fiordland region — one of the most dramatic landscapes on Earth. Stop at scenic viewpoints along the way for photography and exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Milford Sound / Piopiotahi. Board a premium small-group or private overnight cruise on Milford Sound, exploring towering fiord walls, cascading waterfalls, and abundant wildlife including dolphins, seals, and penguins.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight aboard the premium cruise vessel — enjoy a gourmet dinner on the water as the fiord walls rise dramatically around you. Star gazing on the deck in one of the Southern Hemisphere's darkest skies.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — continental spread with fresh fruit, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch on board the cruise vessel — fresh South Island seafood chowder, artisan bread, and local wine
meals.dinner: On-board premium dinner — pan-seared fiordland crayfish, slow-braised beef short rib, and a curated New Zealand wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book the premium Milford Sound overnight cruise well in advance — options include Real Journeys Milford Mariner (luxury cabins available) or a fully private charter. Pack an overnight bag with essentials. The drive from the resort to Milford Sound is approximately 4–5 hours — depart by 7:30am. Bring a waterproof jacket as waterfalls can spray the deck.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up on the water in Milford Sound at dawn — witness the fiord in magical early morning light. Enjoy a gourmet breakfast on board. Morning kayaking directly from the vessel into the fiord — a once-in-a-lifetime experience paddling beneath 1,200-meter granite walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark and depart Milford Sound. Scenic drive back through Fiordland National Park, stopping at Mirror Lakes and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the resort. Enjoy a relaxing hot tub session, followed by a quiet in-room dinner or resort restaurant meal — letting the extraordinary Fiordland experience sink in.

meals.breakfast: On-board gourmet breakfast — eggs cooked to order, smoked salmon, fresh fruit, and premium coffee as the fiord awakens around you
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch for the return drive — artisan sandwiches, fruit, and snacks prepared by the cruise kitchen
meals.dinner: Light resort dinner — fresh green salad, grilled New Zealand salmon, and a glass of Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound kayaking is weather dependent — calm mornings are ideal. Waterproof gear is provided. The return drive offers spectacular photo opportunities — allocate extra time for stops. Arrive back at the resort by approximately 5:00–6:00pm.

day_by_day.morning: Gourmet breakfast at the resort. Depart by private vehicle to the Routeburn Track trailhead. Begin the guided Routeburn Track Day Hike — one of New Zealand's Great Walks — through ancient beech forests, across alpine meadows, and past pristine mountain lakes with a professional guide providing ecological and cultural commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Routeburn Track guided hike, reaching elevated viewpoints with sweeping panoramas over the Humboldt Mountains and Darran Range. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch at a scenic alpine location. Return to the trailhead by private vehicle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Celebrate the day's hike with a premium cocktail at the resort bar, followed by a celebratory dinner featuring the best of South Island cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hearty hiking breakfast at the resort — oats with manuka honey, scrambled eggs, whole grain toast, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet alpine picnic prepared by the resort — smoked chicken wraps, hummus and veggie sticks, trail mix, fresh fruit, and a thermos of premium tea
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining — Otago venison rack with wild mushroom jus, truffle potato gratin, and a Central Otago Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track guided day hike covers approximately 16–25km depending on the section chosen — confirm the route and difficulty level with the guide service in advance. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots and bring layers. The guide will carry emergency equipment. Book through a premium guiding company such as Routeburn Guided Walks for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort. Morning at leisure — optional activities include stand-up paddleboarding on the beachfront, a private photography walk with a local photographer, or a visit to a local artisan market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury 4WD off-road adventure through South Island's backcountry — explore remote high-country stations, cross braided rivers, and discover landscapes rarely seen by tourists. Expert local guide included.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a premium spa experience — choose a couple's massage or a signature treatment. Dinner at the resort's beachfront terrace with a curated degustation menu.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smashed avocado on sourdough, poached eggs, fresh tropical fruit, and cold-pressed green juice
meals.lunch: High-country station lunch during the 4WD adventure — traditional New Zealand farm-style meal with lamb, roasted vegetables, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Resort degustation dinner — 7-course tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring the finest South Island produce including Bluff oysters, Canterbury lamb, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: The private 4WD adventure should be booked through the concierge with a reputable local operator. Wear comfortable, casual clothing suitable for off-road conditions. This is a wonderful day for photography — bring a quality camera or request the resort's in-house photographer to accompany you.

day_by_day.morning: Final full hiking day — early gourmet breakfast, then depart for a premium guided hike in the region. Explore a local hidden gem trail recommended by the resort concierge — perhaps a coastal cliff walk, a waterfall hike, or a forest trail with endemic birdlife including kea, tui, and fantails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the hike and enjoy a farewell afternoon at the resort — swim in the infinity pool, lounge on the private beach, or browse the resort's boutique for New Zealand artisan souvenirs and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest dining venue. Request a personalized menu from the executive chef celebrating the highlights of your South Island journey. Toast to an extraordinary 13-day adventure with a bottle of premium New Zealand sparkling wine.

meals.breakfast: Final hiking breakfast — energy-rich granola bowls, protein eggs, fresh fruit, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Post-hike resort lunch — fresh seafood platter, crisp salads, and artisan bread with New Zealand olive oil
meals.dinner: Farewell degustation dinner — personalized 8-course menu by the executive chef, featuring the best of New Zealand's culinary landscape with a premium wine pairing and bespoke dessert

day_by_day.notes: Ask the concierge to arrange a special farewell touch — perhaps a personalized note from the chef, a bottle of wine to take home, or a curated gift box of New Zealand artisan products. Confirm departure logistics and transfer arrangements for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — take your time and savor every moment of the stunning beachfront setting. Complete packing and check out. Private luxury transfer to the airport arranged by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart New Zealand South Island. If the flight is in the afternoon, enjoy the resort's late check-out option (pre-arranged with the concierge) or spend final hours in the resort's lounge, pool, or beachfront before the transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight — carry with you extraordinary memories of 13 days of world-class hiking, legendary bungy jumps, breathtaking fiords, and unparalleled South Island luxury.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a leisurely spread of your favorite dishes from the past 13 days, enjoyed with a final cup of New Zealand's finest single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge lunch or light bites during the transfer, depending on flight timing
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Arrange late check-out with the resort in advance to maximize your final morning. Confirm private airport transfer timing at least 24 hours before departure. Allow extra time at the airport for any duty-free shopping — New Zealand Manuka honey, local wines, and artisan chocolates make excellent gifts. Ensure all activity GoPro footage, photos, and digital memories are downloaded and backed up before departing.
